summary: Zhang et al. 2025 supply the corpus's boundary-condition evidence: a systematic evaluation across 4 models, 9 benchmarks, and 5 MAD methods finds MAD generally fails to beat simple single-agent baselines CoT and SC, with the failures varying by task type (worse on programming, better on math) and unaffected by hyperparameter tuning. The authors identify model heterogeneity (Heter-MAD) as a consistently effective remedy, improving all tested MAD frameworks, with gains attributed to correcting CW/WC questions. Findings are anchored to PDF pages 1, 3, 7, 9, 11, and 12.
unresolved: Whether Zhang et al.'s null results are specific to the 9 benchmarks or extend to more complex reasoning tasks (they themselves note benchmarks may be too simple).
The exact compute parity conditions (LLM calls vs tokens) across MAD and baselines are not fully specified in this extraction.
